title: Y-Tz-R
hook: yetzer, the impulse, and yatzar, to form, like a potter

segments.voice: Yesterday, B-R-A: bara, the verb the Torah keeps for God. Your line was create. What small new thing did you bring into the room? Today, the verb for shaping what's already there. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-five.

A lump of clay sits on a wheel. It has no idea what it's going to be. The potter's hands close around it, wet, and the wheel spins, and a wall begins to rise. Push too hard and it collapses. Too gently and nothing happens. Hebrew has a verb for exactly this, yatzar, to form, and a potter is a yotzer, a former. From the same root comes a word Jewish tradition uses for something going on inside a person: yetzer, the impulse, the urge. Today's root: yud, tzadi, resh. Y-Tz-R. Clay on the outside, and clay on the inside.
screen: `CLAY ON A WHEEL.` → `YOTZER: A POTTER.` → `Y-TZ-R: TO FORM.`

segments.voice: Turn this root four ways. First, the dust. Yesterday's verb was bara, create. In the second chapter of Genesis the verb changes: "Then the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life." Formed is yatzar. This time the picture is a potter at work: dust, shaped by hand. Second, the two yuds. In the Hebrew of that verse, the word for formed, vayyitzer, is spelled with two letter yuds where one would do. The Talmud, in tractate Berakhot, notices, and reads the two as two impulses: the yetzer tov, the good impulse, and the yetzer hara, the bad one. A person, in this reading, is formed with both. Third, the impulse. After the flood, the text says plainly, "the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth." Imagination there is yetzer. And yet the rabbis refuse to treat it as simply evil. A midrash on the creation story says the urge is part of what God called very good, because without it, nobody would build a house, marry, or raise a family. For these rabbis, the impulse is raw material, not the enemy. Fourth, the wheel. The prophet Jeremiah goes down to the potter's house and watches. A vessel goes wrong in the potter's hand, and he doesn't throw out the clay. He makes it again, into another vessel. Then the word comes: "as the clay in the potter's hand, so are ye in My hand." Formed, and able to be formed again.
screen: `THE DUST: FORMED BY HAND.` · `THE TWO YUDS: TWO IMPULSES.` · `THE IMPULSE: RAW MATERIAL, NOT THE ENEMY.` · `THE WHEEL: FORMED AGAIN.` · then, large: `יָצַר`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: shape one impulse. Settle, and breathe. Notice an urge that's around today. To check your phone. To snap at someone. To eat something. To quit. Don't fight it, and don't obey it yet. Just hold it the way a potter holds clay, as material. Then ask what shape it could take. The urge to snap could become one honest sentence later. The urge to quit could become a real break. Let your hands rest open while you think, as if something soft were in them. The bell holds the time.
Y-Tz-R. Yud, tzadi, resh: the root of yatzar, to form, like a potter, and of yetzer, the impulse a person is formed with. Today's word.
Your line: form. Today, when an urge rises, give it one turn on the wheel before you act. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-five.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching speaks of the yetzer tov and the yetzer hara, the good and bad impulses, and Jewish ethical and Hasidic writings treat the work of a life as shaping and channeling the yetzer rather than destroying it.

original.note: Hebrew: impulse, inclination; from the root of yatzar, to form.

trapdoor: what you thought: the evil impulse is the devil on your shoulder.
what it means: yetzer is the urge a person is formed with, raw material to be shaped.
what a scholar hears: Berakhot 61a reads the two yuds of vayyitzer in Genesis 2:7 as the two impulses, good and bad.

notes: Berakhot 61a reads the double yud of vayyitzer (Genesis 2:7) as two inclinations; confirm the summary.
Genesis Rabbah 9:7 (on 'very good' including the evil inclination; without it no one would build a house, marry or have children) is paraphrased; confirm citation and summary.
Confirm exact JPS 1917 wording of Genesis 2:7, Genesis 8:21 and Jeremiah 18:6 as quoted.
